answer.summary: Duolingo assumed a user’s phone-interface language was the language they wanted to learn from. In India, many users had their phone UI set to English, but were looking to learn English, so the app offered the wrong courses and they left.

sections.heading: What Duolingo misunderstood
sections.content: Gina said Duolingo didn’t realize that many people in India set their phone interface to English, in part because typing in Hindi is hard and India has many languages. The app used the phone’s UI language as the learner’s base language and offered courses in other languages from it. So English-UI users were shown options such as French, Spanish, or German from English, even though they were trying to learn English; they couldn’t find what they wanted and left.
